item.title: Pre-Order Making the Modern Laboratory
item.description: A lavishly illustrated hardcover book about the working laboratory, and how (nearly) everything in it came to be. Featuring 54 essays, many of which have never appeared online.

item.title: Species Have Blurry Boundaries
item.dc:creator: Kevin Blake
item.description: A bacterium can acquire new genes without acquiring a new name, or acquire a new name without changing whatsoever.

item.title: More Stories We'd Like to Publish
item.dc:creator: Editors
item.description: A third installment of articles that we’d like to publish across medicine, biosecurity, the environment, animal welfare and more.

item.title: Great Leaps in Biological Theory
item.dc:creator: Ulkar Aghayeva
item.description: Two of biology’s greatest theories completely predate direct experimental evidence. Tracing their origins could help us understand how to make the next ones.

item.title: On the Role of Theory in Biology
item.dc:creator: Ulkar Aghayeva
item.description: Biology is often seen as a primarily experimental science, with theory serving merely to generalize patterns from empirical data. But history reveals that theory plays a more generative role in the process of biological discovery itself.

item.title: Asimov Press is Back
item.dc:creator: Niko McCarty
item.description: Asimov Press returns with a renewed focus on original reporting, investigations, and thesis-driven philanthropy.

item.title: Antibiotics Are an Economic Failure
item.dc:creator: Matt Burnett
item.description: Social practice and market shortcomings are the bottleneck for solving antibiotic resistance; not molecular discovery.

item.title: A Brief History of Bioinformatics Software
item.dc:creator: Ella Watkins-Dulaney
item.description: How computer scientists on the fringes of biology made sense of sequencing data.

item.title: A Brief History of Lab Notebooks
item.dc:creator: Ulkar Aghayeva
item.description: How experimental recordings have changed, from the Renaissance through today.

item.title: Metaphors for Biology: Evolution
item.dc:creator: Samuel Clamons
item.description: A series of quantitative metaphors on the speeds of representative events in evolutionary biology. The end of our three-part series.

item.title: How to Build a Strep A Vaccine
item.dc:creator: Eva Amsen
item.description: After decades of scientific and regulatory delays, several Strep A vaccine candidates are entering clinical trials. Without further funding for phase 3 studies, however, many will be hamstrung.

item.title: That's All, for Now
